evidence.curator_note: Generic scheme (+)YR-CH2-CH2(.) -> YR(+.) + CH2=CH2: the radical site is on the terminal carbon and the charge stays on the saturated heteroatom (converse of eq 4.9). Book draws 3 arc(s); moves <1,2,3> are ALL drawn on the page -- one electron of the Y-CH2 sigma bond onto Y, the other into the forming C=C bond, and the odd electron of the terminal CH2 into that same bond -- so no implicit hook is required here. Instantiated by the curator as Y = O carrying a second methyl: the book leaves Y's remaining valences open, and a charge-only (even-electron) oxygen needs three bonds, so CH3-O(+)(CH3)-CH2-CH2. is the smallest faithful realisation. This precursor is a distonic ion formed in an earlier step, not the molecular ion itself; ms_context records the EI context and the curator-computed precursor m/z.

rule_index cross-links equation 4.10 to IMS_4_10 ([_A+]1[C]2[C.]3 >> [_A+.]1.[C]2[C.]3). PARTIAL MISMATCH, not support: the left side and the cleaved Y-C bond are correct, but the right side never forms the C=C pi bond and leaves the odd electron on the terminal carbon, so a second unpaired electron is invented (spin 1 -> 2). Verified in the container: applied to CH3-O(+)-CH2-CH(.)-CH3 it returns C[O+.] plus [CH2][CH2.]C, a di-radical fragment instead of an alkene. The rule is therefore dropped at assembly time by the conservation guardrail in rules/__init__.py ('4.10 ... [spin 1->2]'); the faithful DFS would be [_A+]1[C]2[C.]3 >> [_A+.]1.[C]2{=}[C]3. No live rule reproduces this equation. All m/z values here are curator-computed from the instantiation.
No m/z and no intensity are printed for this generic scheme; 46.0413 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of (CH3)2O+. for the chosen instantiation (electron-mass corrected). Not a measurement.
